summary: The strict option defaults to true instead of false, so a project with no strict setting now gets every strict check (noImplicitAny, strictNullChecks and the rest).
An unset module now means esnext; before it meant commonjs under the old es5 default target (es2015 for newer targets).
An unset target now means the latest standard ECMAScript version (es2025 in 6.0, a floating default) instead of es5, so modern syntax is no longer downleveled by default.
noUncheckedSideEffectImports defaults to true instead of false, so a side-effect import of a module that cannot be resolved is an error by default.
libReplacement defaults to false instead of true, so @typescript/lib-* packages in node_modules no longer replace the built-in lib files unless the option is set explicitly.
An unset rootDir now means the directory containing tsconfig.json instead of the inferred common directory of the input files, so src/index.ts emits to dist/src/index.js unless rootDir is set.

An unset types now means [] instead of every package under node_modules/@types, so globals from @types/node, @types/jest and similar are only visible when listed in types (types: ["*"] restores the old behavior).

The computed moduleResolution default for module es2015 through esnext is bundler instead of classic (so the new esnext default resolves as bundler); commonjs keeps node10 and the deprecated module values keep classic.

A function or method that never uses this is no longer treated as context-sensitive during generic inference, so method-syntax callbacks with untyped parameters now infer from sibling properties regardless of property order instead of falling to unknown.

Generic calls and generic JSX elements that take function expressions are checked more strictly (the any-function wildcard is a subtype but no longer a supertype of function types, and JSX children propagate non-inferrable flags), so some calls now report implicit any or need an explicit type argument.
moduleResolution bundler may now be combined with module commonjs; before, that combination was rejected with a program error and bundler required module esnext or preserve.

lib dom now contains everything from dom.iterable and dom.asynciterable, so iterating a NodeList or HTMLCollection works with lib: ["dom"] alone; dom.iterable and dom.asynciterable are now empty files.

Under exactOptionalPropertyTypes, property comparison no longer treats a missing optional property as equivalent to undefined, so { p?: string } and { p?: string | undefined } are no longer identical types.
target es5 is deprecated (an error unless ignoreDeprecations is "6.0"); es2015 is the lowest supported target and ES5 output needs an external compiler.
Setting downlevelIteration at all, even to false, is now a deprecation error where 5.9 accepted it silently; it only ever affected the now-deprecated es5 emit.
moduleResolution node (node10) is deprecated in favor of nodenext or bundler; setting it is an error unless ignoreDeprecations is "6.0".
The module values amd, umd, system and none are deprecated and error unless ignoreDeprecations is "6.0"; ESM or commonjs emit with a bundler replaces them.
The /// <amd-module name="..." /> directive is deprecated together with module amd and no longer has any effect.
baseUrl is deprecated and is no longer a lookup root for bare module specifiers; paths entries must carry the prefix themselves (a "*" catch-all mapping restores the old lookup).
moduleResolution classic is deprecated (an error unless ignoreDeprecations is "6.0"); nodenext or bundler replaces it.
esModuleInterop now defaults to true and setting it to false is a deprecation error, so CommonJS modules are always imported with interop semantics (import x from "m" rather than import * as x).
allowSyntheticDefaultImports now defaults to true and setting it to false is a deprecation error, so default imports from modules without a default export are always allowed for type-checking.
alwaysStrict false is deprecated; all code is parsed as strict mode, so sloppy-mode identifiers such as await, static, private or public are now syntax errors.
outFile is deprecated (an error unless ignoreDeprecations is "6.0"); concatenated single-file output needs an external bundler.
Declaring a namespace with the module keyword (module Foo {}) is a deprecation error; write namespace Foo {} (ambient declare module "x" {} is unaffected).
Import assertions are deprecated: import x from "./a.json" asserts { type: "json" } and import("./a.json", { assert: {...} }) are errors; use the with keyword and the with option instead.
The /// <reference no-default-lib="true"/> directive is deprecated and no longer supported; use noLib or libReplacement instead.
tsc given file arguments in a directory that has a tsconfig.json now fails with TS5112 instead of silently ignoring the config; the new --ignoreConfig flag restores the old behavior.
target es5, deprecated in 6.0, is removed: it is a hard error that ignoreDeprecations no longer silences, and es2015 is the lowest target.
downlevelIteration, deprecated in 6.0, is removed; setting it is a hard error.
moduleResolution node (node10), deprecated in 6.0, is removed and is a hard error; nodenext or bundler replaces it.
The module values amd, umd, system and none, deprecated in 6.0, are removed and are hard errors; esnext or preserve with a bundler replaces them.
The /// <amd-module /> directive, deprecated in 6.0, is removed together with module amd.
baseUrl, deprecated in 6.0, is removed and is a hard error; paths entries must be written relative to the project root.
moduleResolution classic, deprecated in 6.0, is removed and is a hard error.
esModuleInterop can no longer be set to false at all (hard error, no ignoreDeprecations escape); interop import semantics are always on.
allowSyntheticDefaultImports can no longer be set to false at all (hard error, no ignoreDeprecations escape).
alwaysStrict is always true and setting it to false is a hard error; sloppy-mode code is no longer accepted.
outFile, deprecated in 6.0, is removed and is a hard error.
module Foo {} namespace syntax, deprecated in 6.0, is a hard error; only namespace Foo {} is accepted.
The asserts keyword on imports (and assert in import() options), deprecated in 6.0, is a hard error; only with is accepted.
/// <reference no-default-lib /> directives, deprecated in 6.0, are no longer respected at all, including under skipDefaultLibCheck.

The typescript package no longer exports the compiler API: lib/typescript.js and typescript.d.ts are gone and import ts from "typescript" only yields the version; tools must alias typescript to @typescript/typescript6 until a new API ships in 7.1.

Inference through template literal types consumes whole Unicode code points instead of UTF-16 code units, so `${infer H}${infer T}` on a string starting with an emoji yields the emoji and the rest rather than two surrogate halves; type-level string utilities that counted code units break.
The package's engines field requires Node.js >=16.20.0, up from >=14.17 in 5.9 and 6.0.
The tsserver executable and lib/tsserver.js are no longer shipped (bin holds only tsc); editors integrate through the new Language Server Protocol server instead.

In JavaScript files, Closure-era JSDoc forms are no longer recognized: a standalone ? type, module:path namepath types, @class/@constructor, @enum, identifier-named typedefs (/** @typedef {T} */ Name;), function(string): void function types, postfix ! and bare values used as types (write typeof v).

In JavaScript files, constructor functions (this.x inside a function plus prototype assignments), fallback initializers (f.x = f.x || v), nested undeclared expandos (N.X.Y = {}), typed this.x; declarations without an initializer, this aliases (var that = this) and top-level this as globalThis are no longer treated as declarations; use classes and explicit assignments.

In CommonJS JavaScript files, nested undeclared exports (exports.N.X.p = 1), an ignored empty module.exports = {}, this as an alias of module.exports, var x = require("m").prop, aliasing module.exports to a variable and mixing module.exports = ... with module.exports.x = ... are no longer supported, and repeated exports.x assignments union instead of narrowing.

Types and symbols are ordered by a deterministic content-based algorithm (6.0's stableTypeOrdering flag) and this cannot be turned off, so union member order in declaration emit and hovers, and occasionally inference results, differ from 6.0's default ordering by type ID.
Conflicting declarations are reported at every contributing declaration instead of sometimes only one, so conflicts that skipLibCheck previously hid entirely now surface in non-.d.ts files.
Declaration (.d.ts) emit from .js input files is rewritten and no longer matches 6.0's output, especially when the input has errors; supported JSDoc tags keep their semantics.

JSDoc in .js files follows TypeScript rules: a variadic {...T} is only an array synonym and no longer makes a parameter a rest parameter, {T=} no longer adds undefined when strictNullChecks is off, an asserts return annotation on an arrow must go on the variable's @type, @typedef and @callback in a class body hoist out of it, a @param applies to at most one function, @type assertions block narrowing, and @overload is ignored on arrow and function expressions.

Calls in .js files use TypeScript's arity rules: with strict false, arguments for parameters typed undefined, unknown or any can no longer be omitted, and using arguments inside a function body no longer implies a ...args: any[] parameter.
